title: conservatory-batcher-and-quant-mapper-cli
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces the Conservatory batcher CLI and quantization mapper: tenant-aware batch templates, telemetry-driven quant profile synthesis, and a dry-run simulator for unit-econ validation. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
description: Motivation: We've seen recurring manual tuning cycles where SREs and platform engineers iterate on batching/caching defaults and quant profiles for tenants with diverse traffic shapes. This PR adds a developer-facing CLI (conservatory) and a backend service helper (quant-mapper) that automate a conservative, tenant-safe rollout of batch/cache defaults and corresponding quantization recommendations. Implementation summary: added a CLI that ingests a tenant workload snapshot, runs a lightweight simulated scheduler to propose 3 ranked batch shapes (latency-first, cost-first, balanced), emits safe cache TTLs and KV-prefill heuristics, and synthesizes a per-tenant quant profile hint file. The quant-mapper translates model + shape signatures into a shortlist of quant variants (int8/ptq/q4_0-like presets) along with expected token-cost deltas and a simulated quality delta estimate based on stored eval reps. Safety model: conservative default uses a "no-quality-regression" gate — unless the tenant opts into a progressive candling rollout that allows small quality delta tradeoffs for cost. The PR also wires telemetry hooks to attach unit-econ delta estimates to traces.

review_comments: Diego Rivera (review): This is great direction. Two asks: 1) make the default safe gate explicit (what happens when evaluator data is missing?), 2) add a small acceptance test that exercises the apply path against a noop backend.

Maya Chen (author): Added a fallback: if eval reps are missing we default to conservative quant presets (no PTQ) and annotate suggestions with 'needs-eval'. Also added a CI smoke that runs the --dry-run path in Docker to catch regressions.
Priya Nair (review): The telemetry tags look good. Please ensure the unit-econ estimator emits both per-token and per-request deltas so billing-team can triage anomalies.
Maya Chen (author): Emitted per-request and per-token deltas; added integration test that verifies metrics appear in the trace payload (ci/conservatory-smoke.yaml).
Liam O'Connor (approve): Approving pending minor nits fixed in follow-up commit.
CI bot: workflow/conservatory-smoke passed on rerun (flaky network on first run).

user_guide_snippet:
Usage: conservatory --tenant <tenant-id> --snapshot path/to/snap.json --mode balanced --dry-run
Example: conservatory --tenant payment-service --snapshot snapshots/pay-svc.json --mode cost-first --apply
Notes: conservatory respects feature-flag 'conservatory.enable' and will not apply changes unless explicitly run with --apply and the tenant has opt-in policy.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Core serving path unchanged until --apply is used. Main risk is incorrect quant suggestion causing quality regression; mitigations: 'no-eval => conservative preset' fallback, staged canary, per-tenant rollback via the CLI.
changelog_entry: Added Conservatory CLI (conservative batcher + quant profile mapper). Provides tenant-safe batch and quant suggestions and a dry-run simulator to validate unit economics prior to apply.
notes_for_releasers: Feature is behind 'conservatory.enable' flag. Coordinate with infra to enable telemetry ingestion for unit-econ traces before wide rollout. Notify billing and SRE teams of planned canary tenants.
qa_steps: 1) Run: conservatory --tenant test-tenant --snapshot tests/fixtures/tenant_workloads.json --mode balanced --dry-run and verify output contains 3 ranked shapes
2) Run: conservatory --tenant test-tenant --snapshot tests/fixtures/tenant_workloads.json --apply --mode balanced against staging backend and verify feature-flag gating prevents apply on production
3) Validate traces: check unit_econ_estimator tags appear in span payloads after a dry-run
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the mapper heuristic small (lookup+parametric) to make future ML-driven profile synth pluggable. A follow-up will add a simulation harness that runs candidate quantizations against a clipped eval subset (ENG-4521).
